Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; one-negative margins therefore cannot establish top-10 ranking quality ([Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). RecSys 2025 research separates sampling reliability into model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with fully observed preferences. These are distinct properties: changing negative sampling can change conclusions without improving preference modeling ([Pereira et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). Research on sampled estimators also identifies difficulty recovering small-K metrics ([Jin et al., 2023](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25561)).

Recommended diagnostic design, inferred from this evidence: keep the host’s 99-negative, seed-42 evaluator unchanged. Compare conditions on identical users and fixed candidate panels; record positive rank, HR@10, and the margin between the positive score and the tenth-highest negative score, with explicit tie handling. Report rank-8–12 cases and hit/miss transitions. Separate auxiliary panels varying sample size and uniform versus popularity sampling quantify sensitivity; full-catalog unseen-item ranking, where affordable, measures a different evaluation setting. Stratify by training-derived target popularity and history length, reporting sample counts. Neither auxiliary panels nor training-prefix diagnostics replace host validation.

Across the three predefined training conditions, predefine expected diagnostic directions, then compare their changes against per-category and macro validation HR@10 changes. Use paired user bootstrap resampling within each category, preserving condition pairing and equal category weights, to estimate uncertainty in differences. Three condition-level observations cannot establish predictive validity; correlation is exploratory, and user resampling does not measure training-seed uncertainty. Preserve single-model GRU4Rec inference and use no test labels.
